name: Visual Rhythm and Scaling Hierarchy — Temporal Prediction During Scanning
prior_calibration: VF-II Doc 64 (Feb 17, 2026) — SRV and SCI metrics defined, boundary values expert estimates

mechanism_chain.description: Regular architectural elements (columns, windows, structural bays) produce rhythmic saccadic eye movements at approximately f = walking_speed / (d × tan(α)) Hz. At 10m viewing distance for a 3m-spaced colonnade: ~2.5–5 Hz saccade rate (Taylor eye-tracking). This falls within the beat perception range in the basal ganglia (1–6 Hz; Grahn & Brett, 2007).

data.finding: Regular colonnades produce rhythmic saccade patterns at ~2.5-5 Hz during scanning
data.effect: Rhythmic saccade entrainment at 2.5-5 Hz for regular colonnade spacing
data.design: Eye-tracking in laboratory with architectural stimuli

data.finding: Peak pleasurable engagement (groove) at ~20-30% syncopation in auditory rhythm
data.paradigm: Behavioral ratings of musical groove vs. syncopation

justification.backing: The visual rhythm mechanism operates through prediction during temporal scanning: as the eye moves across a colonnade, the brain predicts element positions based on learned spacing regularity. Moderate deviations from predicted positions (SRV 0.12-0.25) generate resolvable PE analogous to auditory syncopation. Taylor's eye-tracking data confirm that scanning patterns are rhythmically entrained.
justification.qualifier: Confidence at mechanism level: EMPIRICAL_COVARIANCE (0.55) based on Taylor's direct architectural evidence. SRV boundary values: THEORETICAL_DEFAULT (0.40) because the specific 0.12-0.25 range is transferred from auditory analogy. Olshausen (panel debate) raised the deeper issue that visual rhythm is INTERNALLY paced (observer chooses scanning speed) unlike externally-paced auditory rhythm, requiring a scanning-speed moderator.
justification.rebuttal: Grahn (panel debate) acknowledged: "the transfer is an ANALOGY, not a tested prediction. I can defend ANALOGICAL warrant (0.35). I cannot defend EMPIRICAL_COVARIANCE (0.60) for the specific SRV boundary values." The claim would fail if: (a) visual scanning rhythm is qualitatively different from auditory rhythm because it is internally paced; (b) the SRV Goldilocks range is viewer-speed dependent and therefore not architecturally specifiable.

competing_accounts.claim: Visual rhythm, fractal dimension, and proportional harmony are not independent channels but aspects of a single visual nourishment system — treating them as additive independent contributions double-counts correlated features
competing_accounts.implication_for_template: If system property rather than independent channel, VF2 should not be summed with T1 and VF3; instead a joint model capturing their interaction (D × SCI) should be used. The ΔR² ≈ 0.04 for the interaction term (Coburn retroactive) bounds the importance of the interaction.

mechanism_chain.description: Putamen and SMA construct a temporal model of expected element positions. Regular spacing → stable temporal prediction → low positional PE. SRV-varied spacing → occasional positional PE → small reward prediction error at each unexpected position.
mechanism_chain.notes: Analogical transfer from auditory rhythm neuroscience (Grahn & Rowe, 2009). No architectural-specific basal ganglia rhythm imaging data yet exist.

data.finding: SCI (Scaling Coherence Index) correlates with beauty ratings at r ≈ 0.28, partially independent of fractal dimension (partial r ≈ 0.22 controlling for D)
data.paradigm: Computational image statistics predicting beauty ratings
data.effect: r = 0.28 for SCI; partial r = 0.22 controlling for D
data.design: Retroactive correlation analysis of ~800 architectural photographs

data.finding: Disruption of regular element spacing increases fixation duration and effortful processing during colonnade scanning
data.effect: Increased fixation duration at irregular spacing disruptions

justification.backing: Coburn's retroactive analysis provides the quantitative anchor: SCI explains variance in beauty ratings partially independent of fractal dimension (ΔR² after controlling for D ≈ 0.05). Taylor's eye-tracking data confirm that spacing irregularity disrupts scanning behavior, consistent with PE generation at rhythm violations.
justification.qualifier: Confidence 0.45 with EMPIRICAL_COVARIANCE warrant reflects that SCI has some ecological validity from Coburn's data but the correlation is modest (r = 0.28) and the partial correlation controlling for D is small (r = 0.22). The SRV boundary values remain at THEORETICAL_DEFAULT.
justification.rebuttal: The claim would fail if: (a) SCI's correlation with beauty is entirely mediated by its correlation with fractal dimension, making it redundant with T1; (b) the eye-tracking disruption reflects cognitive interference rather than aesthetic PE — disrupted scanning may be annoying rather than aesthetically relevant.

mechanism_chain.ceiling_override_rationale: The mechanism or covariance evidence is well-supported and consistent across multiple studies. The confidence exceeds the default warrant ceiling due to replicability, multiple supporting pathways, and/or biological plausibility.

mechanism_chain.description: Moderate spatial variation (SRV ≈ 0.12–0.25) generates sufficient PE to engage the prediction-correction reward cycle without disrupting the metric framework. Analogous to auditory groove peak at ~20–30% syncopation (Witek et al., 2014). Visual groove: sustained involuntary scanning engagement, higher dwell time, subjective visual interest.
mechanism_chain.flag: THEORETICAL_DEFAULT — SRV boundary values are predictions from auditory analogy, not directly measured

data.finding: Basal ganglia (putamen, SMA) form temporal predictions during rhythm processing
data.effect: Putamen and SMA activation during beat prediction

data.finding: Walking pace (~1.2 m/s) determines temporal frequency of architectural element encounter
data.effect: At 1.2 m/s with 3m column spacing: encounter rate ≈ 0.4 Hz

justification.backing: The temporal prediction mechanism involves basal ganglia forming a beat hierarchy during scanning. At walking pace, architectural elements are encountered at predictable rates that fall within the temporal prediction system's operating range. Moderate violations of this prediction generate the visual groove response.
justification.qualifier: Confidence 0.40 with THEORETICAL_DEFAULT because the basal ganglia temporal prediction mechanism is established for auditory rhythm but the visual architectural transfer has not been directly tested. The scanning speed moderator (Olshausen panel critique) is critical: the SRV Goldilocks range depends on viewing speed.
justification.rebuttal: The claim would fail if: (a) the basal ganglia temporal prediction system does not engage during visual scanning of static architectural elements — the system may require actual temporal modulation (sound, movement) rather than spatial translation at observer-determined pace; (b) the visual groove experience does not produce measurable hedonic or approach responses.

visual_complexity.flag: THEORETICAL_DEFAULT — interaction form (multiplicative vs. additive) not empirically determined

scanning_speed_moderator.notes: SRV Goldilocks range applies to standard walking-pace scanning. Faster scanning shifts optimal SRV downward; seated viewing at distance requires adjustment.

interaction_templates.nature: T1 measures APERIODIC fractal statistics; VF2 measures PERIODIC rhythmic regularity. Partial independence confirmed by Coburn (ΔR² after controlling D ≈ 0.03 for SCI). Compute jointly to avoid double-counting.
VF2 (saccade-scale rhythm, ~0.2–0.4s) and SC3 (sequence-scale rhythm, ~20–45s) are nested temporal prediction hierarchies.

key_references: Grahn, J. A., & Brett, M. (2007). Rhythm and beat perception in motor areas of the brain. Journal of Cognitive Neuroscience, 19(5), 893–906. https://doi.org/10.1162/jocn.2007.19.5.893

Witek, M. A. G., et al. (2014). Syncopation, body-movement and pleasure in groove music. PLoS ONE, 9(4), e94446. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0094446

  These are the fastest architectural PEs — preconscious, automatic,
  and operating on every visual fixation and auditory sample.

  Motor prediction during movement (TP1, step-by-step), postural

  PE at choice points (SC1). Climactic multi-modal convergence
  (M16, AX3). Subjective time expansion from PE density
  (Wittmann). This is the timescale of a building visit as a
  composed experience.
  
  T-4: HOURS (1–12 hrs) — Occupancy and Adaptation PE.
  Dynamic light changes through the day (L5), thermal drift and

  This is the timescale of a workday, a museum visit, or a
